label: the crawler (models/headcrab.mdl): a sludge crawler: low, wet, six-legged, the size of a headcrab, grey-green with a pale belly and a ring of teeth

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/chumtoad.mdl, models/roach.mdl, models/leech.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked C, D, D, A where the asset was B, B, B, D: passed for one of the game's
measured.contract: keeps the headcrab's bones, animations, attachments and bodyparts

M1.reason: Against the brief's words (low, wet, six-legged, headcrab-sized): the body is a low dome, about 12 units tall against 27 long, and the legs splay evenly from it. Side, back, top and below views all show the same low, flattened outline, and no part sticks out of place.

M2.reason: The brief gives no figure, only 'the size of a headcrab', and sizeAsked is null, so there is no number to hold the 26.4 x 27.7 x 12.2 measure to within 15%. The lineup's three Half-Life models are small (leech, roach, chumtoad), so they are no check on size. Nothing in the pictures is clearly off, but the size is not verified.

M3.reason: Parts listed from the brief: six legs (top and below views each show three legs per side), a ring of teeth round the front mouth (front view and front-left/front-right views show a red disc with a ring of pale teeth), and a pale belly (the below view and the side views show it under the body). All are present in their places. Nothing from the list is missing.

M4.reason: The body is grey-green, the belly is pale, and the mouth ring is dark red with pale teeth. Those are the brief's colours and materials, with no region in the wrong colour.

M5.reason: The brief asks for no markings beyond the teeth and the pale belly, and both are there. The plain faceted skin adds nothing wrong, and the mouth's teeth stay sharp at the sizes shown.

M6.reason: Fixed at 2 by the rubric's cap. The line-up was run four times in four orders with the asset at B, B, B and D; the judges picked C, D, D and A, so the asset was taken for one of the game's each time.

M7.reason: The front is the mouth ring, facing the front view. It stands upright on its legs, and in the run frames its feet sit on the floor line. Nothing is turned or lying on its side.

M8.reason: 448 triangles against a Half-Life median of 308, so the limit is 616 (twice the median; three quarters under 340, so the larger bound applies). checkErrors is empty. The belly plate and mouth look closed in the views, and the legs stay attached in the jump frames and the walk frames.

C1.reason: Walk frames 0 to 34 and jump frames 0 to 30 are drawn frame by frame from the side. The legs stay joined to the body and move with it, and the mouth ring stays on the front. The body rotates in the jump without any part coming apart, sinking, or floating. (The second sheet is labelled JUMP, so the attack is a leap.)

C2.reason: The contract line reads that it keeps the headcrab's bones, animations, attachments and bodyparts, so the game's own headcrab plays it. No compareContract result appears in the measurements, so this rests on the contract line.
